Brief-claimed-by: session_01KrKXQVvgYk2AJ4VkqMobyb · batch #400 · 2026-10-26T14:07Z

Director seat, summon #51 continuation (ledger objectstack#12708). Presented to the maintainer in batch #400 as its one item (the card entered the box at 13:50Z, after batch #399 was presented). Seat increment (re-verified on `origin/main` `cdd4eea9`; the card's analysis is not restated):
- Premises hold: `RUN_LIFECYCLE_DENY_VERB` appears in `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts` (cancel is the operator verb of #13953; ADR-0044:164–166 records `cancelRun` as the engine's first run-cancel primitive, consuming the continuation and logging terminal `cancelled`); the resume door's admission is `isRunStarterOrRunStateReader` (`:259–284`, #19987); `FlowRunner.tsx:624` closes the dialog with `onClose()` only, no request. PR #26134 (the first half of #25801, `type: 'file'` screen field) is open, draft, +959/−48; #25801 is `pm:dispatched`, spec p1.
- `git grep -iE 'abandon|discard run'` on the runner and `packages/spec/src/automation` → 0: no abandon verb or UI exists today, so any of A/B/D is a new REST verb or a new config key (the card's protocol line is right).
- Execution shape for the card's own recommendation (B, staged): a staged B has no machine-readable restart condition ("the first screen flow that must write mid-run" is a judgement), so under the state model it is not a `pm:on-hold` card — the ruling records the direction and this card closes `not_planned` with the ruling as its record, reopened free when such a flow appears; #25801 closes on #26134 with a pointer here. The seat states this so the letter decides the direction and the close at once.
- Facets read: same direction; the seat agrees with **B, staged** (direction: the starter may abandon their own paused screen run after a confirm; not built until a real mid-run-writing screen flow exists — zero pull once #26134 lands). Not A (silent loss on a mis-click), not C as an end state (no exit for the starter), D as a separate operations question if paused runs accumulate. Workload now: 0; when picked up, spec lane · 1 PR (runtime verb + console confirm), no precedent.
Prior rulings read: `RUN_LIFECYCLE_DENY_VERB` · `#13953` · `#19987` · `ADR-0044 cancelRun` → the operator-only cancel stance and the starter-open resume door; thread: none (new card).

Ruling: batch #401 item 1 (batch #400's open item) · letter B, staged · maintainer 「同意」 2026-10-26T17:34Z

Recorded by the director seat (summon #51 continuation, `session_01KrKXQVvgYk2AJ4VkqMobyb`, ledger objectstack#12708, brief 6418049443). Letter **B, staged**. Direction: the starter of a paused screen run may abandon it — closing the dialog asks "abandon this run?", and only a confirmed answer calls a new starter-scoped abandon verb (the run's pre-dialog writes are not rolled back; cancel stays the operator verb of #13953 / ADR-0044). Not A (silent loss on a mis-click), not C as an end state, D as a separate operations question if paused runs accumulate. Timing: not built now — the only measured pull (hotclm#99 item 4) was removed by PR #26134 (merged: a `type: 'file'` screen field lets a wizard move every write past its last screen), and no screen flow that must write mid-run exists in this repository or in hotclm; a new verb is a permanent REST and permission surface, added when such a flow exists.

Closed `not_planned` with this ruling as the record: a staged letter has no machine-readable restart condition, so it is not a `pm:on-hold` card; reopening is free the day a real mid-run-writing screen flow appears, and the implementation card then cites this comment (`Ruling-ref:`). #25801 closes on #26134 with a pointer here (the spec seat's act).

Workload of the chosen letter: 0 now; spec lane · 1 PR (runtime verb + console confirm) when reopened, no precedent.
